testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle with dual air brakes, the pressure should reach ____ before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build pressure to at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about ____ to your total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Not be used by the driver.
Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. Open the manual air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What should happen if air pressure in the brake system falls below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light should come on.
Lights should flash on the outside of the vehicle.
A message should appear on the control panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light should come on.
questions.explanation: A low air pressure warning light comes on if pressure falls below 60 psi. On large buses, it may come on at 80 to 85 psi.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made after March 1, 1997, and other air brake vehicles made after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Brakes may get out of adjustment:
questions.explanation: Brakes can go out of adjustment quickly, especially if overheated. Check brake adjustment regularly.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet weather below freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze so the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze so the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: Using the parking brake in very wet weather below freezing can cause the brakes to freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is:

options.text: Used when transporting both liquids and gases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used when transporting both liquids and gases.
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to drive a tank vehicle that transports liquids or gases. This includes both hazardous and non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into storage tanks. It stops pumping when pressure gets too high and starts pumping when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: You can brake only if there is enough air left in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
Drive normally and check the brakes when you have time.
Keep driving but turn on emergency flashers to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can brake only if there is enough air left in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and park your vehicle safely as soon as possible. Your brakes will work only as long as there is enough air in the tanks.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat. This overheating causes brake fade, which makes the brakes less effective at slowing the vehicle.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?

options.text: If they are used at all.
If one side is used more than the other side.

questions.explanation: Hot brakes are likely to get out of adjustment. Use proper braking methods to keep your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, how much air can a triple combination vehicle with air brakes lose in one minute?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 5 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repair and should not be driven.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum air loss for a double combination vehicle in one minute?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test. Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle.

questions.question: Which gauge shows how much air pressure is in the tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: Do not drive if a brake drum has a crack larger than ____ of the friction area width.
questions.explanation: Check your brake drums during your walk-around inspection before each trip. Do not drive if any brake drum has a crack larger than one half the width of the friction area.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It is not available for vehicles with air brakes.
It is not helpful in most driving situations.
It helps you maintain control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you maintain control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with air brakes and help drivers keep control by preventing the wheels from locking up.

questions.question: Where are the ABS warning lights located on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with ABS have yellow warning lights on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS warning lights on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: How do you apply the parking brake in a newer vehicle?

options.text: By using a diamond-shaped yellow knob
By using a round red knob
By using a square green knob
By using a black round knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a diamond-shaped yellow knob
questions.explanation: In a newer vehicle with air brakes, pull the diamond-shaped yellow knob to apply the parking brake. Push it in to release the parking brake.

questions.question: How should you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels
Apply the brakes with about half-force
Apply the brakes until the wheels lock

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brakes, steer, then brake again.

questions.question: What are air tank drains used for?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks
Remove water and oil from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too noisy
Other braking systems are hard to find

questions.explanation: When used and maintained properly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.
